english.title: Fail to co -operate with the provision of a specimen of breath - preliminary test - aviation offence
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed, without reasonable excuse, to co -operate with a preliminary test in pursuance of a requirement imposed by section 6 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 as modified by section 96 of the Railway and Transport Safety Act 2003
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 96 and 95 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
having been required to provide a preliminary test
without reasonable excuse failed to do so

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence wording is to be used for offences relating to aircraft. See also the corresponding offence wordings relating to ships H5621 and mechanically propelled vehicles H5623.

other.powersofarrest:
Under section 6D(2) a constable may arrest a person without warrant if -
(a) the person fails to co -operate with a preliminary test in pursuance of a requirement imposed under section 6, and
(b) the constable reasonably suspects that the person has alcohol or a drug in his body or is under the influence of a drug

N.B. In (b) above, failure to give a breath test is, in itself, insufficient grounds to arrest, the officer must also have a belief that the suspect has alcohol in his/her body.
other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
